author: NASASpaceflight
description:
China is making rapid progress toward reusable rockets—but its latest success came with an unexpected twist. LandSpace’s ZhuQue-3 successfully completed its first orbital booster landing before apparently tipping over on the pad shortly afterward.

Meanwhile, NASA has officially ended its attempt to save the aging Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory, bringing one of astronomy’s most successful space telescopes closer to its final reentry.

Also this week:

🚀 ZhuQue-3 becomes China’s latest reusable rocket success

🌙 LRO discovers the fresh crater left by a Falcon 9 upper stage impact

🛰️ Firefly announces a future Blue Ghost Radioisotope Heater Unit

🌕 NASA may finally replace Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter

🔭 Hera reveals how Deimos was reshaped by an ancient impact

🇷🇺 Ukrainian strikes may disrupt Soyuz rocket production

🚀 ESA studies reusable Phoenix 3 while The Exploration Company advances Nyx

📈 Falcon 9 reaches another historic booster landing milestone

📅 Plus everything coming up n
